text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- Sergei Dubinin, the Chairman of Russia's Central Bank, has started playing a difficult game, the daily says after Dubinin accused a commercial bank of misappropriating governemnt funds.

- Boris Berezovsky, named by Forbes as the richest man in Russia, is expected to make his income public by Wednesday according to a presidential decree authorising government officials to report their incomes.
- The communist opposision definitely lost the regional elections on Sunday in central Russia.
- Russia has resumed palladium exports to Japan after a seven-month pause.
- The "Russian food" trading company, 50 percent of which belongs to Russia's state-controlled Sberbank, is planning to take part in the sugar for oil tender scheduled for September.
- Foreign investors seem to have failed to win seats on the board of directors of Novolipetsk Metallurgical Plant at the weekend meeting of shareholders.
SEVODNYA

- Officials at a Moscow meat processing plant are admitting the possibility they received "madcow" beef from Belgium from March to April 1997, but they say it was all processed and sold three months ago.
- Two Chechen travel agencies are planning to open direct flights from Grozny to Istanbul and Dubai on July 17.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA

- The problem of the Baltic states will affect Russian-German relations in the future, says the paper on the eve of German Foreign Minister Klau Kinkel's visit to Moscow, referring to the possibility of the three former Soviet republics receiving an invitation to join NATO.
- A group of atomic workers marching in protest against wage delays has reached the outskirts of Moscow and is planning to picket the government building on Thursday and Friday.
- Russia received $3.5 billion exporting arms last year and is planning to increase revenues up to $9 billion by the end of this year, says "Rosvooruzheniye" general director Alexander Kotelkin.
- Russia's biggest bank scandal won't go away by itself and may lead to sad consequences for both the companies and personalities involved in the conflict, says the paper.
IZVESTIA

- Former first deputy finance minister Andrei Vavilov's career as president of the International Company for Finance and Investments (IFCI), which he moved to after leaving the ministry, is under threat, the paper says.
- Western humanitarian aid to Russia is held up by the unecessary bureaucracy of customs officials.
- Two officials from the company producing Sukhoi-37 fighters are sacked after some technical failures during the June air show at Le Bourget.
ROSSIISKAYA GAZETA

- The central bank head has accused commercial bank Unikombank of misappropriating half a billion dollars in government money said some finance ministry officials had broken the rules in dealing with it.
- The military has started to receive the money the government promised to pay back by September 1, says a Defence Ministry official quoted by the official government paper.
- Police fail to fight prostitution since it does not exist under Russian law, says the paper.
ROSSISKIYE VESTI
- The opposition has lost its battle on the Volga, says the presidential paper, commenting on the provisional results of Sunday's election in the central Nizhny Novgorod region.

- Leonty Shevtsov, former commander of Russia's contingent in Bosnia, and Valery Yevnevich, head of the Dnester group of Russian troops in Moldova, are among possible candidates to take over the post of head of Russia's interior troops.
KOMSOMOLSKAYA PRAVDA
- Justice Minister Sergei Stepashin talks about reforms at the ministry in a front page interview.
--Tatyana Ustinova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520.
